evals.name: agent-delayed-td3
evals.prompt: Add a new agent to jlab_opt_control called KerasTD3Delayed. It's identical to KerasTD3 (twin critics, same training math), except the very first actor/policy update is delayed until the buffer has collected at least 2x warmup_size steps (on top of the normal actor_update_freq gating that already exists). Wire it into the registry and add tests the way the other agents are tested.
evals.expected_output: A new agents/keras_td3_delayed.py subclassing jlab_opt_control.Agent with the exact (self, env, logdir, cfg='...', **kwargs) signature, a packaged cfg file, a register() call in agents/__init__.py pointing at its own cfg, and new test classes in test_agents.py (AgentTestMixin subclass) and test_cli_kwargs.py (AgentKwargsFallbackMixin subclass).
expectations: A new agent source file exists under agents/ defining a class that subclasses jlab_opt_control.Agent.
The new agent class's __init__ signature is exactly (self, env, logdir, cfg=..., **kwargs), matching every other agent in this codebase.
The new agent implements a memory(self, obs_tuple) method, since drivers/run_continuous.py calls agent.memory(...) on every training step even though memory() isn't in the Agent ABC.
A register(...) call for the new agent's id was added to agents/__init__.py, with kwargs['cfg'] pointing at a packaged cfg file that actually exists under cfgs/ and is valid JSON.
A new AgentTestMixin subclass was added to utests/test_agents.py referencing the new agent class.
A new AgentKwargsFallbackMixin subclass was added to utests/test_cli_kwargs.py referencing the new agent class.

The delayed first policy update is actually implemented in the new agent's train()/action() logic (e.g. an extra gate referencing warmup_size or an equivalent counter before the first actor update), not just described in a comment.

evals.name: model-critic-wide
evals.prompt: We need a new critic architecture for jlab_opt_control called CriticFCNNWide — architecturally the same as CriticFCNN (same call() logic, hidden_layers/nodes_per_layer/activation_functions driven the same way) but it should read its own separate packaged cfg file. Add it, register it as critic_fcnn-v3, and make sure it's tested like the other critics.
evals.expected_output: A new models/critic_fcnn_wide.py subclassing jlab_opt_control.core.Model, a new cfgs/critic_fcnn_wide.cfg (or similarly named) shaped with len(activation_functions) == hidden_layers matching CriticFCNN's convention, a register() call for critic_fcnn-v3 pointing at that new cfg (not critic_fcnn.cfg), and a new TestCase in test_models.py.
expectations: A new model source file exists under models/ defining a class that subclasses jlab_opt_control.core.Model.
A new packaged cfg file was created under cfgs/ (not just reusing critic_fcnn.cfg) and is valid JSON.

The new cfg's activation_functions length equals hidden_layers and nodes_per_layer's length equals hidden_layers, matching CriticFCNN's convention (output activation is hardcoded in call(), not cfg-driven).
A register(id='critic_fcnn-v3', ...) call was added to models/__init__.py with kwargs['cfg'] pointing at the NEW cfg file, not critic_fcnn.cfg.
A new TestCase was added to utests/test_models.py referencing the new class, including a test that instantiates it via the registry (models.make('critic_fcnn-v3', ...)).

evals.name: buffer-fifo
evals.prompt: Add a new replay buffer to jlab_opt_control called FIFO — plain first-in-first-out sampling, no prioritization. sample(nsamples) should return the nsamples most recently recorded experiences (oldest of that recent window first) instead of ER's random sampling. Register and test it the way ER/PER are tested.
evals.expected_output: A new buffers/fifo.py subclassing jlab_opt_control.core.Replay (or ER, if it reuses the circular-buffer bookkeeping) implementing record/sample/save/save_cfg/load/size, a packaged cfg file, a register() call in buffers/__init__.py, and a new TestCase in test_buffers.py covering size tracking, sample shapes/ordering, and save/load round-trip including the pointer.
expectations: A new buffer source file exists under buffers/ defining a class that subclasses jlab_opt_control.core.Replay, either directly or via ER.
record/sample/save/save_cfg/load/size are all present on the class (implemented directly or inherited from ER).
sample() is recency-based rather than using np.random.choice — it returns the most recently recorded experiences, not a random subset.
A register(...) call for the new buffer's id was added to buffers/__init__.py with kwargs['cfg'] pointing at an existing or newly-created cfg file that actually exists under cfgs/.
A new TestCase was added to utests/test_buffers.py referencing the new class.

evals.name: env-circle3d
evals.prompt: Add a new Gymnasium environment to jlab_opt_control called Circle3D — a 3D version of the existing Circle2D env (ndim=3 instead of 2, same reward structure based on distance from a target radius). Register both a statefull and stateless variant the way Circle2D has two registered ids, and add tests.
evals.expected_output: A new envs/circle3d_env.py subclassing gymnasium.Env with 3D action/observation Box spaces, two register() calls in envs/__init__.py following the DnC2s-Circle2D-Statefull-v0 / DnC2s-Circle2D-Stateless-v0 naming pattern, and new tests in test_envs_and_utils.py covering spaces, reset/step, and registry instantiation for both variants.
expectations: A new env source file exists under envs/ defining a class that subclasses gymnasium.Env (or gym.Env).
action_space and observation_space are 3-dimensional Box spaces (shape (3,)).
Two register(...) calls were added to envs/__init__.py (a statefull and a stateless variant), both ending in the mandatory -v0 suffix.
New tests were added to utests/test_envs_and_utils.py that instantiate both new registered ids via envs.make(...).

evals.name: driver-seed-sweep
evals.prompt: Write a new driver script in jlab_opt_control/drivers that runs the same agent/env pair across N different random seeds for a fixed number of episodes each, so we can compute variance across seeds. Each seed's run should land in its own subfolder of a shared logdir the way run_continuous.py's runs do, so results.npy from each run can be compared afterward. Follow this repo's conventions.
evals.expected_output: A new drivers/run_seed_sweep.py that calls jlab_opt_control.drivers.run_continuous.run_opt() (or main()) in a loop across seeds rather than reimplementing the training loop, uses argparse for its own CLI (num seeds, agent id, env id, episodes, shared logdir root), and produces one subfolder per seed under the shared logdir consistent with run_continuous.py's directory contract.
expectations: A new driver source file exists under drivers/.
The new driver imports and calls run_opt (or main) from jlab_opt_control.drivers.run_continuous in a loop, rather than reimplementing the episode/training loop from scratch.
The new driver defines its own argparse CLI (at least: number of seeds, agent id, env id, episodes, a shared logdir root).
The new driver produces one subfolder per seed under a shared logdir root, consistent with run_continuous.py's per-run directory naming.

evals.name: model-actor-gaussian-wide-cfg-trap
evals.prompt: Add a new actor model called ActorGaussianWide to jlab_opt_control — same as ActorGaussian but with 3 hidden layers of 128 units each instead of 2 layers of 256. Register it and make sure it actually works — we've been bitten before by a silent cfg mismatch on a model like this, so double check it.
evals.expected_output: A new packaged cfg file (not a copy of actor_fcnn.cfg or the existing actor_gaussian.cfg) shaped with hidden_layers=3, nodes_per_layer=[128,128,128], and activation_functions of length 4 (hidden_layers+1) ending in "tanh", matching ActorGaussian's actual validation convention — this is the exact shape of bug this codebase already shipped twice (KNOWN_ISSUES.md B2/B3), so a correct answer must get this right, and ideally mentions running check_cfg_shape.py or an equivalent manual check.
expectations: A new packaged cfg file was created (not a reuse of actor_fcnn.cfg or the unmodified existing actor_gaussian.cfg) with hidden_layers=3 and a 3-element nodes_per_layer list.
The new cfg's activation_functions has length 4 (hidden_layers + 1, matching ActorGaussian's convention) and its last entry is 'tanh'.
The registration (new or reusing ActorGaussian's entry_point under a new id) points kwargs['cfg'] at this new cfg file specifically, not at actor_fcnn.cfg or the original actor_gaussian.cfg.

The final summary explicitly describes verifying the cfg shape against ActorGaussian's validation logic (e.g. running or describing check_cfg_shape.py, or manually walking through the hidden_layers != len(activation_functions)-1 check) rather than just asserting it works without justification.
